notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.20.2 prints two formats: Format 1, MULTIPLY identifier-1 or literal-1 BY one or more identifier-2, each with an optional ROUNDED; Format 2, MULTIPLY identifier-1 or literal-1 BY one identifier-2 or literal-2 GIVING one or more identifier-3, each with an optional ROUNDED; both end with the ON SIZE ERROR phrase, then the NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase, then END-MULTIPLY, each optional. The superset rule multiplyStatement parses both, and BindMultiply narrows the BY operands per format at every edition: Format1Receivers refuses a literal BY operand written without GIVING, GivingSendingOperand a second BY operand or a ROUNDED on it written with GIVING (COBOL1689). The one later addition to the operands, ROUNDED MODE IS, is refused at 85 by VisitRoundedPhrase (COBOL0803). All of that was probed at --std 85. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is one the statement's formats print and is not yet written, with no edition arm, so the NOT phrase written before its positive twin compiles and runs at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 (item 33), which the row's change record names. Same mechanism as the ADD, SUBTRACT, STRING and UNSTRING rows of this slice. The witness runs both formats with the phrases in the printed order.

next.reason: 1985: "{ identifier-2 [ ROUNDED ] } … [ ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "{ identifier-2 [ rounded-phrase ] } with choice indicators: zero or more, each at most once, in any order; ROUNDED [MODE IS …]". 2023 accepts more programs: ROUNDED may take MODE IS with eight modes, and NOT ON SIZE ERROR may come before ON SIZE ERROR. In 1985 the order was fixed.
